Honestly this game just feels like a content update for Dark Survival but bundled and marketed as a 'new game' to expand the franchises library. I'm quite disappointed to be frank. It play's the exact same, story and all, like as if it were a copy and paste of Dark Survival but with added re-skinned mechanics. Within the 5 hours I've played (which is definitely more than enough) the thing that impressed me the most were the glow sticks to keep track of explored area's. Had this game just been a free update for Dark Survival I wouldn't be disappointed at all, but the fact it built up a lot of hype for the past few weeks plus in Secrets of the Machine, is really rubbing me the wrong way, which the franchise already has been for the past couple years. I often think back to one quote TheMeatly said during a Q&A for Batim, 'I don't wanna milk this dry/I don't wanna do this just because I can turn out Bendy stuff all the time'. Really starting to seem otherwise now. I hate to be negative but for a franchise I hold so close; seeing it's (in my opinion) fall from grace, I feel like I had to be honest. On a side note, nice of the dev's to make this free for people who own Dark Survival. But dear god $20?! I can't defend that.

I bought BatDS and although I haven't played it much, I can compare it to BLW and say that the game has a lot of content. But at the same time, it has a lot of problems. For example, the level generation and Bendy's behavior, which together make Hard Mode basically impossible. There are dead ends, long corridors without safe booths, sometimes even items don't spawn (items for the elevator ride, I mean) #FixGenerations

"Now, let's sell the same game once again, but for x7 the price, and with a bit of new content!" Lone Wolf not only doesn't fix any of the problems that original game has, but also amplifies them. Generation was not thought out, it's made of same chunks for each floor, so you can easily get 2 stamina refills for a whole level, or 4 for 3x3 area. Main enemy, being Bendy, aka Ink Demon, hasn't changed a bit. He's still cluncky and useless as before, mostly serving purpose of atleast somewhat making gameplay have more action. Whole studio fears Ink Demon, even in BATIM butcher gang dies solely from his presence. But here, he's just a chasing dummy who doesn't interact with the world at all, and who can be looped around a single pillar. The mighty Ink Demon, is now just a child who plays tag. I mean, what developer hasn't ever wanted to break their own canon for sake of not wasting 2 hours on making enemies die around him, and at best 3 hours for integrating some animations of him interacting with a world? That's right, the one that cares about their fans. Combat was unnecessary, as it has 2 moves and that's it. So when more than 1 enemy attacks you, you're guaranteed to get a few hits. Locations are all bland, and each one has the same way to find items, which becomes boring. When we first heard of combat, and upon entering the game saw abillity to switch weapons, we though: "wow, so cool! I can find a weapon that fits my playstyle!". Turns out, all of the weapons are the same thing, just different skins. It would be atleast great, if they had their own animations (that are GOOD, and where you'd feel the impact of hitting enemy). But no, devs decided 2 animations for the whole game are enough for you. I could name so many more reasons as to why this game is lazy, like poor optimization with lack of graphical settings, not even being able to change controls, bland locations, etc. But this pathetic cash grab doesn't even deserve me wasting any more time on this review. I'll play a few more hours, and maybe my opinion will change once I find different enemies and bosses. But for now, this game is lazy. The devs just want your money, that's it. DON'T BUY THIS GAME, LIKE SERIOUSLY, DON'T!

A sort of upgraded/remade version of Boris and the Dark Survival. Those not familiar with BatDS, it is a spin-off isometric procedurally generated fetch quest game. The original did not have much focus. You would go to a floor, collect the necessary items, maybe get a collectible, escape. It’s really simple, kind of unfair, and very boring. This upgrade now gives more of a progression system, some new minigames, and actual stand-alone level areas. What makes the previous iteration and this unfair is that you are constantly being hunted by the invincible ink demon (or relating boss). There are two things to note, one the layout of any level is randomly generated so you can very easily get stuck in a long hallway with a dead end and no where to hide. The second is that the moment you grab the last necessary item, you WILL be chased. Meaning, yet again, you can very easily be cornered with very little response to do. To add to the nuisance your sprint, blocks, and attacks all use an ink gauge that runs out with use. So general navigation can easily be cumbersome particularly with the random/limited ink refill stations. I’d also like to note it’s incredibly stupid you have to worry about your ink gauge when you are in your hub area. Enemies have inconsistent stun phases and fighting more than one can lead to wonky encounters. Collectibles being a random drop added to the fact that the containers they are found in are also randomly generated is just… so awful. All bosses that you can fight are the same and there is no depth to engagement. Recommend? The Bendy series has been one disappointment after another and this is no exception.

Not a bad dungeon crawler. Combat is fine, simple, exactly what it needs to be, in my opinion. It's easy to get sucked into its simple and repetitive gameplay loop, and there are plenty of collectibles for the many secondary objectives you need to keep an eye out for while playing. The game is built entirely on you spending your time searching for the secondary collectibles to advance towards the game's many endings, as opposed to searching for the supplies that you only use to finish the level. The controls are responsive and simple, and while I haven't finished it myself yet, the game apparently contains interesting story moments that lead up towards the next in the Bendy series. If you like Bendy, you'll definitely get a lot more out of it than the average player, pretty much purely because it's just more stuff to do in this interesting world. I don't really have any negatives to list, purely because it's such a simple game. You either like it, or you don't, really.
